name: Belian Earth
summary: belian.earth builds locally-trained, project-specific counterfactual baselines for nature-based carbon projects (ARR, REDD+, IFM). For ARR under VM0047, its ramet47 platform narrows the comparison area using satellite embeddings, then matches project and control plots on a stocking index.
production: Two satellite embedding products (ESD from Landsat+MODIS, 2000-2024; AlphaEarth from Sentinel-1/2, Landsat and GEDI, 2017 onward) predict top-of-canopy height (RH98) and canopy density (PAI), calibrated to NASA GEDI lidar. Both are resampled to a 30 m grid and fused into one annual, gap-free series using inverse-variance weighting, a temporal Kalman smoother and breakpoint detection, with AlphaEarth weighted higher from 2017. Low-confidence pixel-years are down-weighted, not discarded.
correlation: Four lines of evidence: held-out GEDI test (geographic split) with RH98 r2 about 0.72, RMSE about 2.5 m; swisstopo airborne-lidar canopy height, r 0.83-0.92; cross-comparison with CTrees biomass (r2 about 0.68-0.73, 2012-2024) and ESA CCI Biomass; and recovery of the benchmark on the first issued VM0047 project (VCS 5511). Local field plots, studies or inventory data are used where available. SI is not provided where correlation cannot be shown.
limits: SI is supplied only where SI-AGB correlation can be evidenced for the forest type or ecoregion; otherwise it is not provided for that area. SI carries only the relative benchmark; absolute tonnes need field plots.
limitations: SI carries only the relative benchmark (absolute tonnes need field plots). RH98 sits about 5-6 m above airborne-lidar canopy height (absorbed in calibration). The CTrees comparison is a consistency check, not ground truth. Pre-2013 Landsat-7-era data are down-weighted.

name: CYCLOPS
summary: US-incorporated dMRV company built on dClimate's EarthOS. For VM0047 it provides an annual 10 m aboveground-biomass map used as the stocking index, and supports the full workflow from eligibility and dynamic baseline to the PDD and monitoring report.
production: Sentinel-2 (and Sentinel-1 in TESSERA) time series are condensed by a self-supervised foundation model into gap-free per-pixel representations. A model trained on GEDI (or airborne LiDAR where available) predicts structure, converted to AGB (t/ha) with an ecoregion-specific factor, giving annual 10 m maps. Imagery is limited to a peak growing-season window, cloud-masked (SCL, s2cloudless) and median-composited; pixels with too few valid observations are flagged, not gap-filled.
correlation: Per project, the forest type and ecoregion are compared with the model's training strata, then R2, RMSE and bias are reported. If the stratum is under-represented, SI is withheld until independent references (airborne LiDAR, GEDI L4A, inventory plots) show correlation. Hold-out data are re-evaluated annually per ecoregion. TESSERA canopy height gave R2 0.78 against airborne LiDAR (N. California); AGB was checked against agroforestry plots in Para, Brazil.
limits: SI is withheld for forest strata under-represented in the training data until local correlation is shown with independent reference data; delivery is suspended if correlation falls below about R2 0.6.
limitations: GEDI training coverage is about 50 degrees N-S (ICESat-2 used elsewhere); strata under-represented in training need an extension assessment before SI is released; pixels with too few valid observations are flagged, not gap-filled.

name: Lobelia Earth
summary: Barcelona-based company using Earth observation, climate modelling and AI. For VM0047 it supplies yearly 10 m maps of aboveground biomass, canopy height and canopy cover (2016 to present) with uncertainty ranges, delivered by API with automated project-control plot matching.
production: A biome-specific deep-learning (UNet) model fuses airborne lidar and GEDI with Sentinel-1/2, land cover and DEM data to map AGB, canopy height and canopy cover at 10 m each year from 2016. Imagery is restricted to biome-specific growing seasons with under 30% cloud cover; clouds, shadows and snow are masked (SCL) and a yearly median composite is built. Outputs include 5th-95th percentile uncertainty.
correlation: Peer-reviewed validation (Perpinya-Valles et al., 2025) in four biomes gives Pearson r of 0.61-0.77. Per project, SI is benchmarked against local GEDI L4A footprints, cross-validated with national forest inventory data or project field plots, and explainable-AI analysis shows which sensors matter locally. SI is delivered only where correlation is statistically verified.
limits: SI is provided only where the correlation with AGB is statistically verified for the project's forest type and ecoregion.
limitations: Pearson r of 0.61-0.77 against reference data in the validation study (four biomes), so uncertainty is material; it is reported as 5th and 95th percentile confidence intervals.
deliveryNoApi: Via Lobelia's own API (job-based): outputs at three levels (raw yearly rasters, plot-level and reporting-level metrics), written to Lobelia's S3 bucket or the client's bucket.

name: TerraCarbon
summary: Advisory firm that helps develop carbon projects for natural climate solutions, from early feasibility to registration and monitoring. For VM0047 it builds a project-specific stocking index, matches project and control plots, and delivers a traceable performance benchmark.
production: Annual composites of Landsat, Sentinel-2 or HLS (SAR if optical is unavailable) over a 10-year history and a 100 km buffer, using the most cloud-free 3 months (widened to 6 if needed). A stocking index suited to the forest type is built from them, e.g., NDFI plus a disturbance-age model, and checked against field data where possible. Plots are about 3x3 pixel groups.
correlation: Case by case, using field data from the project area or ecoregion whenever possible. In an illustrative Brazilian eucalyptus case, an NDFI + disturbance-age model reached R2 of about 0.80-0.84 against stem-volume plots. Optical and SAR saturation is assessed per project.
limitations: Optical data saturate within 1-3 years in eucalyptus plantations; L-band SAR saturates at about 100-200 t/ha; the SI metric is therefore chosen project by project.
deliveryNoApi: To client and VVB: matching criteria, SI time-series raster, matched project/control plots, Excel workbook, written description and R/Python code.

name: Treefera
summary: AI-native intelligence platform for agricultural and soft-commodity supply chains, including forest cover, biomass and carbon. For VM0047 it provides an annual NDVI stocking index from Landsat (30 m, since 2000), an ARR eligibility checker, and performance monitoring and benchmarking.
production: NDVI is computed per pixel from Landsat 5/7/8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance (Microsoft Planetary Computer). Scenes up to 80% cloud are kept, clouds and shadows are masked with the QA band, same-day tiles are mosaicked, and each cell's annual value is the mean of valid pixels at 30 m (2000 to latest year, 2012 excluded). A harmonic regression then separates seasonal cycles from trend.
correlation: NDVI has a peer-reviewed correlation with AGB. For each project we show three lines of evidence: published NDVI-AGB relationships for the biome; proponent field plots used to cross-validate at plot-footprint scale; and independent AGB references where available. Correlation is reported with uncertainty. It weakens in high-biomass closed-canopy forest, which we flag.
limits: Needs at least 10 years of pre-start history and 30 project plots (0.81 ha each); 2012 is treated as missing; NDVI saturates in high-biomass closed-canopy forest (flagged).
limitations: NDVI saturates in closed-canopy forest; Landsat only (Sentinel-2 under evaluation); 2012 missing; Table A1 overlays not applied; Step 4 control revalidation not implemented.

name: TransparenC
summary: Geospatial analytics for carbon markets: 100+ automated data layers for feasibility, due diligence and digital MRV. For VM0047 it supplies stocking index data (AGB or EVI) and a dynamic baseline built from a donor zone and matched control pixels.
production: AGB: a project-specific machine-learning model (gradient boosting / random forest) is trained on Google Satellite Embedding V1 (or Clay embeddings from Sentinel-1/2 for sub-yearly use) paired with GEDI-derived AGB, at 10 m. EVI: derived from Landsat at 30 m. Both use a consistent annual window of at least four low-cloud months (typically June-September) applied the same way every year.
correlation: Where possible the Sentinel-2/GEDI AGB product is used directly and its test error, bias, RMSE, R2 and cross-validation are reported. For EVI, proponent plots are used to check the link with biomass; otherwise published regional evidence, quality-filtered GEDI observations or held-out samples are used. We stratify or recalibrate where the relationship is weak.
limitations: EVI is more sensitive to seasonal variation than GEDI-derived AGB. The EVI-biomass link may be weak in some areas and then needs recalibration or stratification. Models are project-specific.
deliveryNoApi: GeoTIFF rasters and vector files, reproducible code, a methodology report and an interactive viewer.

name: Varaha
summary: Nature-based carbon removal developer across South and Southeast Asia and West Africa, with deep ARR and agroforestry expertise. Its MRV stack combines multi-sensor satellite data, machine learning and field plots to deliver tree-cover, land-use and biomass datasets for VM0047.
production: Annual Sentinel-2 composites (bands 2, 3, 4, 8; 20 m bands resampled to 10 m) are built from cloud-masked scenes in agro-ecological-zone seasonal windows (South Asia: typically Nov-Feb), with Sentinel-1 filling cloud gaps and DEM-based illumination correction. Pre-2017 years use harmonised Landsat at 30 m, cross-calibrated to Sentinel-2. Outputs carry metadata, valid-pixel counts and quality flags.
correlation: Four steps: classify the project ecoregion and forest type; establish project-specific sample plots (tree inventory converted to plot AGB with local allometry); fit a project-specific SI-AGB regression with k-fold and spatially-blocked cross-validation (R2, RMSE, MAE, bias, residual diagnostics); benchmark against literature and propagate uncertainty. A validation report accompanies each SI.
limits: Operating countries listed: India, Nepal and Bangladesh; the seasonal windows described are for South Asia.
limitations: Persistent monsoon cloud (mitigated by dry-season compositing and SAR), topographic shadow in mountains (DEM correction, residual uncertainty reported), and Landsat-Sentinel-2 cross-sensor harmonisation for pre-2017 years.
deliveryNoApi: SI delivered with metadata, valid-pixel counts, quality flags and a project-specific SI-AGB validation report.

name: Sylvera
summary: Independent carbon data platform offering ratings, pricing intelligence and geospatial lidar monitoring. Its Biomass Atlas gives annual aboveground biomass maps; for VM0047 it supplies donor pools, stocking-index rasters, matched plots and annual benchmark results.
production: Annual Landsat (5/7/8/9) composites from all cloud-free observations feed a bias-corrected regression that uses satellite-derived canopy height to predict aboveground biomass (Mg/ha), trained on airborne laser scanning and multi-source lidar with separate ecoregion models. A pixel-level temporal profile model (constant, linear, B-spline, change-point) suppresses seasonal noise and fills gaps so every pixel has an annual value.
correlation: AGB is the model's primary output, so no secondary SI-to-AGB correlation step is needed. Training labels come from ALS and multi-source lidar, converted to AGB with allometry validated against destructive field plots, and separate models per ecoregion fit the AGB-height relationship to each forest type.
deliveryNoApi: Donor pool in GIS format, SI raster inputs with metadata, project/control plots with full boundaries, and benchmark results in a spreadsheet.

name: Kanop
summary: Kanop uses AI and satellite data to measure climate and biodiversity impact. Its deep-learning models give aboveground biomass at 10 m and 30 m globally, and it offers end-to-end VM0047 services: dynamic baseline, stocking index, ex-ante estimates and PDD support.
production: A deep-learning model trained on about 125 Mha of LiDAR reference data predicts AGB (Mg/ha). 30 m product: Landsat + PALSAR + SRTM DEM (2013-2025). 10 m product: adds Sentinel-1/2 (2017-2025). Optical composites use the greenest months (MODIS NDVI), cloud-masked and BRDF-corrected (median of the least cloudy 60%); LandTrendr on NBR stabilises mature forest; PALSAR-2 dry-season mosaics give HH, HV and RVI.
correlation: SI is AGB itself (Mg/ha). The model is trained on about 125 Mha of structural reference data (42 Mha airborne LiDAR, 83 Mha GEDI); global site-level validation gives R2 0.65 against LiDAR-derived AGB. Optional project recalibration with field measurements (Gaussian Process Regression fusion, inverse-variance weighting) gives a default 95% confidence interval.

name: Chloris Geospatial
summary: Chloris Geospatial uses machine learning on multi-satellite data to estimate aboveground biomass stock, biomass change and forest cover change. For VM0047 it supplies an annual AGBD stocking index (2000-2025) and a full dynamic baselining workflow.
production: Landsat acquisitions are aligned to a fixed 30 m grid, corrected to NBAR reflectance, and masked with the Landsat QA layer plus a custom cloud mask. A machine-learning model (Baccini et al. method) predicts AGBD using all imagery in the target year plus context from previous and subsequent years. Maps are reprojected to a regional equal-area projection, keeping 30 m pixels.
correlation: Comparison with GEDI shows strong correlation across all Olson biomes; independent validation includes NEON field plots (R2 = 0.76), USFS FIA plots (R2 = 0.90) and Brazilian airborne-lidar biomass transects (R2 = 0.74-0.90). For each project, correlation is shown with customer field measurements, public regional datasets or GEDI-derived biomass.
limitations: Some cloud contamination can remain even after QA masking; Chloris applies its own custom cloud mask to reduce it.
